claim: The data firmly support the involvement of PDZ-RhoGEF in the genetics of fat mass regulation and predisposition to obesity and T2D.
source: Our data firmly support the involvement of PDZ-RhoGEF in the genetics of fat mass regulation and predisposition to obesity and T2D, previously suggested by the association of the PDZ-RhoGEF SNP R1467H with the epidemiology of T2D (Bottcher et al., 2008; Fu et al., 2007; Jin et al., 2010; Liu et al., 2011; Ma et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript states this conclusion based on their findings and cites prior work.

claim: Further work on determining the nature of the PDZ-RhoGEF H1467R SNP variant is needed to fully understand its action in obesity and T2D predisposition.
source: Further work on determining the nature of the PDZ-RhoGEF H1467R SNP variant, using functional reconstitution of PDZ-RhoGEF KO cells and mice, as well as biochemical characterization of its activity towards RhoA will be needed to fully understand its action in obesity and T2D predisposition.
evidence: The manuscript provides this statement about future work needed.
